notes:
- **See who is fixing your mod**: every repair now says who is doing it. A green **Auto-Healer** card means the app fixed it by itself - no AI, no tokens - and lists each fix. An indigo **AI repair** card means the Assistant is fixing it with tokens, with the attempt number and the cause of the crash. A slim bar above the message box shows the live status ("Auto-Healer · compiling to check 2 automatic fixes", "AI repair · checking the AI's fix - starting Minecraft"), with **Details** to open the Activity panel.
- **Crashes fixed without AI**: the Auto-Healer now repairs the "Duplicate DefaultAttributes entry" crash by itself. When two classes register the same mob's attributes, it keeps the registration in your mod's common code, comments out the second one (backed up first) and starts the game again. If it can't decide, the AI gets the exact file and line of every registration, so it no longer guesses at a file it can't see.
- **Repair without AI first on Build & Run**: the Auto-Healer switch is now in the Run settings card on Build & Run, next to Auto-fix build errors and Verify after every change.
- **3D Studio: every animation on its own**: asking for "run, walk and attack - very scary" now makes three separate animations named run, walk and attack, instead of one animation called "attack walk run". An animation that already exists is redone and improved, not duplicated as "walk 2".
- **3D Studio: new Animations list**: see every animation of your mob with whether it loops and how long it is. Click one to play it, tick animations to **Redo** or **Delete** them, or press **+ New** to describe more.
- **3D Studio: choose what to change**: Look & motion has **What to change** - **Whole mob** (model and animations), **All animations** (keep the model) or **Checked only** (redo just the animations you ticked). The main button says exactly what it will do, e.g. "Redo 2 checked animations".
- **Better animations**: the AI now follows a professional motion guide - bigger, readable movements, a wind-up before every attack, follow-through on the head, tail and wings, and style words that really change the motion ("scary" means jerky twitches, a hunched body and reaching arms).
